item.title: What we are about
item.dc:creator: arir71302
item.content:encoded:
We understand how difficult it is for students to find quality healthy food around university, with roadblocks such as prices, distance and quality. Our aim is to increase the awareness of students of access to healthy, affordable and varied food options.

The University of Herts has a big campus and a limited range of food options available to students, especially when it comes too healthy eating, that is why we have made this website in order to help make it easier on students.

item.title: Meal Plans
item.dc:creator: alonzoanaeme
item.content:encoded:
These example meal plans show how a student could organise a week's food around different budgets. Each plan is designed for one person and uses ordinary supermarket ingredients, leftovers and a mix of plant and animal protein.

University project prototype: prices are illustrative weekly grocery-budget estimates per student, not fees for supplied meals. Actual supermarket costs vary by store, portion size, location and dietary needs. Herts Active does not currently sell or deliver food.

Choose a meal-plan budget

Basic Meal Plan

Estimated weekly grocery budget

£25 / week

A low-cost plan built around oats, eggs, beans, lentils, rice, pasta, frozen vegetables and leftovers.

  • Low-cost cupboard staples
  • Batch-cook friendly meals
  • Simple breakfasts and lunches
  • Vegetarian swaps for most dinners
See example week

Premium Meal Plan

Estimated weekly grocery budget

£35 / week

A varied weekly plan with more fresh produce and a mix of chicken, eggs, beans, dairy and vegetarian meals.

  • More variety across the week
  • Fresh and frozen vegetables
  • Flexible protein options
  • Leftovers planned for next-day lunches
See example week

Exclusive Meal Plan

Estimated weekly grocery budget

£45 / week

A more flexible example plan with extra choice, fish or alternative proteins, varied vegetables and a few convenience options.

  • More meal variety and choice
  • Fish, chicken and plant-based options
  • Additional fresh ingredients
  • Planned snacks and easy lunch options
See example week

Basic: example week

Repeat ingredients across meals to reduce waste. Use frozen vegetables and swap beans, lentils or eggs for meat where preferred.

Premium: example week

Exclusive: example week

A few practical notes

  • Cook larger portions of rice, beans, chilli or curry and chill or freeze leftovers safely.
  • Use frozen fruit and vegetables where they are better value or easier to store.
  • Choose water as your everyday drink and adapt meals to your appetite, allergies and dietary needs.
  • These are examples, not medical or dietetic advice. Follow any individual advice from a qualified health professional.

For general balanced-eating guidance, see the NHS Eatwell Guide. It explains how to balance food groups over a day or week rather than expecting every single meal to be perfect.

Recipe inspiration

Find simple recipes and cooking ideas on the Healthy Recipes page. The example menus above can be adapted to suit vegetarian, vegan or other dietary preferences.

item.title: Welwyn Garden City
item.dc:creator: alonzoanaeme
item.content:encoded:
Welwyn Garden City has lakeside parkland, free outdoor exercise spaces and a large sports complex. This guide highlights a few ways to get active, whether you prefer a walk, a community run or organised sport.

Photo: Welwyn Hatfield Borough Council.

Stanborough Park

Stanborough Park is a major outdoor recreation area in Welwyn Garden City, with lakeside paths and activities around the water. It is also the venue for Stanborough parkrun, a free weekly 5K where people can walk, jog, run, volunteer or spectate.

Stanborough parkrun: Saturdays at 9:00am, at Stanborough Park, Stanborough Road, Welwyn Garden City, AL8 6DF. It is free, but participants should register with parkrun before their first visit and bring their barcode.

Council event information · Stanborough parkrun website

King George V Playing Fields

Welwyn Hatfield Borough Council has installed outdoor gym equipment here, including hand-bike and recumbent-bike equipment designed to be accessible to a range of users. The council also reports that the multi-use games area has an upgraded surface and can be used without advance booking.

Read the council's outdoor-gym update

Gosling Sports Park

Gosling is a large sports venue on Stanborough Road. Its current facilities listing includes a gym, fitness studios, tennis courts, golf driving range, ski centre, football pitches, sports hall, squash courts, cycling velodrome and athletics track. Some activities require booking or payment.

Check Gosling Sports Park facilities and booking

item.title: St Albans
item.dc:creator: alonzoanaeme
item.content:encoded:
St Albans offers a mix of historic parkland, walking and cycling routes, leisure-centre facilities and organised sport. Here are a few useful places to explore if you want to keep active around the city.

Photo: St Albans City and District Council.

Verulamium Park

Verulamium Park is a 175-acre public park close to the city centre. St Albans City and District Council notes that it holds both Green Flag and Green Heritage Site awards. The park sits on the site of the Roman city of Verulamium, and remnants of the city walls and London Gate can still be seen nearby.

It is a good place to consider for walking, relaxed outdoor exercise and cycling. The park also connects visitors with local heritage and Verulamium Museum.

Official Verulamium Park information

Leisure centres and sports facilities

Westminster Lodge Leisure Centre

The council's sports directory lists a swimming pool, gym, group exercise and sports hall at Westminster Lodge. It is a useful option for indoor training and classes.

Address area: AL1 2DL · Tel: 01727 736 080

Check facilities, classes and current opening times

Abbey View Sports Complex

Abbey View is listed by the council among the district's sports venues. Nearby Verulamium Park also has playing pitches and beach-court facilities, with availability and booking managed by the relevant operators.

Check Abbey View Sports Complex · Council playing-pitches directory

Ideas for an active day in St Albans

  • Walk or cycle through Verulamium Park.
  • Look into a gym session or group class at Westminster Lodge.
  • Check the council's sports directory for football, cricket and other pitch facilities.
  • Combine outdoor exercise with a visit to the local Roman heritage sites.

For current opening times, facility access, classes and booking arrangements, use the venue or council links rather than relying on old listings.

item.title: Free Workouts
item.dc:creator: alonzoanaeme
item.content:encoded:
Move more,Spend less

Free Workouts: Get fit without spending money

We are realise the struggles and difficulties of being on top of your finances and being able to afford the most basic necessities, working out shouldn't be one of them. There are plenty of ways working out can be done from home where you are always on top of your fitness. Students already have a lot to think about so we have quick and easy fitness routines to help.

Home Workouts -

Exercises like squats, pushups and planks are a good foundation into building strength and muscle for beginners, a well rounded workout for students who are looking to start their fitness journey.

Cardio-

Cardio is a very important aspect when it comes to health as its needed for stamina, endurance and it strengthens the heart which is important for students as they typically have busy workloads. Its very good for students as well, as it can help keep them active while being on top of university. This can help them with studies or extra-curricular activities.

Yoga & Streching

A very important aspect to young students as most students who attend Herts Uni have a very sedentary lifestyle, due to the amount of work that they are given. Yoga is a great way to relax and stretch the muscles minimizing the risk of back pain, knee pain and more commonly eye strain. It gives students a way to still be active without having too leave the room.

item.title: Privacy & Cookies
item.dc:creator: alonzoanaeme
item.content:encoded:
This page explains the cookies and analytics technologies used when you visit Herts Active, a student fitness and wellbeing project website hosted on WordPress.com.

Last reviewed: 10 November 2026. Herts Active is a university project. It does not currently sell products, run advertising campaigns or operate its own user-tracking platform.

1. What are cookies?

Cookies are small files stored by a website in your browser. Similar technologies, such as tracking pixels and browser storage, can also be used to remember settings or measure how a website is used.

2. Essential WordPress.com cookies and technologies

Herts Active is hosted by WordPress.com. WordPress.com may use essential cookies or similar technologies to provide and protect website services, such as account sign-in, security, spam prevention, comments and other features you choose to use. These are provided and managed by the hosting platform rather than by a separate Herts Active tracking system.

The exact cookies set can depend on whether you are signed in to WordPress.com and which features you interact with. For the platform's current cookie details, see Automattic's Cookie Policy.

3. Website analytics: WordPress.com / Jetpack Stats

WordPress.com provides built-in Jetpack Stats on this site. It is already enabled by the hosting platform; Herts Active has not added Google Analytics or a separate analytics plugin. Stats help the project understand which pages and guides are being viewed so that content can be improved.

Jetpack Stats uses a small tracking pixel that loads in the visitor's browser. Depending on the activity and settings, it can record:

  • Post and page views.
  • Video plays for videos hosted by WordPress.com.
  • Clicks on links that lead away from the website.
  • Referring website addresses and search-engine terms.
  • Broad location information, such as country (and, where available in the service, region or city).

To produce these statistics, Automattic says the underlying data can include an IP address, WordPress.com user ID and username if the visitor is signed in, browser or device user-agent, the page visited, referring URL, event time, browser language and country code.

What the Herts Active team can see: the site owner sees summary statistics, such as total views, popular pages and traffic sources. WordPress.com states that information directly identifying a particular visitor, such as their IP address or WordPress.com account ID, is not visible to the site owner through Stats.

How long the underlying logs are kept: Automattic states that Stats logs containing visitor IP addresses and WordPress.com usernames, where available, are retained for 28 days and used to power the Stats feature. On the WordPress.com Free plan, the site dashboard provides a limited recent-history view of basic traffic statistics.

More information is available in the WordPress.com Stats documentation and the Jetpack privacy information.

4. Advertising and third-party analytics

Herts Active has not intentionally added Google Analytics, advertising pixels, remarketing tags or a separate marketing analytics service. The site is on the WordPress.com Free plan, so WordPress.com may display its own platform promotions or apply platform-level technologies under its own terms and privacy information.

When you follow a link to an external website, that website's own privacy and cookie practices apply. Herts Active does not control those external services.

5. Your choices and an important Free-plan limitation

WordPress.com provides a Cookie Consent block for block themes, but its banner has an Accept button and does not provide a Reject button. WordPress.com says a third-party consent plugin is needed for a visitor-facing reject option; installing third-party plugins is not available on this site's current Free plan.

WordPress.com also states that site owners cannot disable Jetpack Stats on the Free plan, and its hosted Stats service does not currently provide a site-level visitor opt-out control. For these reasons, Herts Active has not added an accept-only banner that could suggest visitors have a choice that the current hosting setup cannot fully honour.

You can use your browser's privacy and cookie controls or privacy extensions to restrict some cookies and tracking technologies. This may also affect sign-in, comments or other website features. Browser controls are not a substitute for a properly configured website-level consent or objection mechanism.

Project limitation: this page explains the current WordPress.com Free setup; it does not claim that the site has a full cookie preference centre or that every visitor can opt out of site analytics from within Herts Active. If the project later moves to a plan that supports a suitable consent-management tool, the team should configure and test an Accept / Reject / Settings workflow before adding optional analytics or marketing services.

6. Changes to this page

This page should be reviewed whenever the site adds a new embedded service, analytics tool, advertising feature, form provider or other technology that stores or accesses information on a visitor's device.

Useful references: UK Information Commissioner's Office guidance on storage and access technologies · WordPress.com Cookie Consent block documentation.

item.title: Healthy Recipes
item.dc:creator: shahrierpritom
item.content:encoded:
Healthy eating as a student does not have to be complicated. These recipe ideas use accessible ingredients, can be adapted to different budgets and offer a mix of vegetarian and vegan options. Select a recipe to see the full instructions from its original publisher.

Recipe note: Herts Active provides short descriptions and links, not the original recipes. Follow the publisher's full method, ingredients and allergen information before cooking.

Four student-friendly ideas

Greek-style beans

About 25 minutes · Vegetarian

A quick butter-bean and tomato stew finished with feta, lemon and herbs. Serve with toast for a filling lunch or dinner.

Main ingredients: butter beans, tomatoes, onion, garlic, feta and herbs.

View full recipe

Peanut butter noodles with tofu & veg

About 30 minutes · Vegan

A protein-rich noodle bowl with tofu, edamame and green vegetables tossed in a peanut and sesame sauce.

Main ingredients: tofu, noodles, edamame, greens, peanut butter and soy sauce.

View full recipe

Quick tomato soup with cheesy garlic dippers

About 25 minutes · Vegetarian option

A warming tomato soup paired with toasted, cheesy garlic bread. Useful for a quick lunch or an easy evening meal.

Main ingredients: tomatoes, onion, stock, bread, cheese and garlic.

View full recipe

Sweet potato & peanut curry

About 60 minutes · Vegan

A comforting curry with sweet potato, peanut butter and warming spices. Make a larger batch and keep portions for another day.

Main ingredients: sweet potato, peanut butter, coconut milk, curry spices and vegetables.

View full recipe

Eating well on a student budget

  • Plan two or three dinners that share ingredients to reduce waste.
  • Use frozen vegetables and tinned beans where they are better value.
  • Cook extra portions and refrigerate or freeze leftovers safely.
  • Adjust recipes for allergies, dietary needs and personal preferences.

For general healthy-eating guidance, see the NHS Eatwell Guide. For example weekly menus and budget tiers, visit Meal Plans.

item.title: Reviews
item.dc:creator: shahrierpritom
item.content:encoded:
Great workouts demand great fuel, but eating healthy as a student doesn't have to mean bland food, hours in the kitchen, or spending your entire budget on specialty ingredients.

True fitness starts on your plate. Every meal is an opportunity to energize your body, sharpen your focus for lectures, and recover stronger after a session at the gym or park. You don't need to be a Michelin-star chef to cook smart—just a few simple, fresh ingredients and recipes designed to fit a busy student lifestyle.

If you don't think so, our reviews tell us otherwise.

item.title: Fuel Your Ambition: Eat Well, Live Well
item.dc:creator: shahrierpritom
item.content:encoded:
Great workouts demand great fuel, but eating healthy as a student doesn't have to mean bland food, hours in the kitchen, or spending your entire budget on specialty ingredients.

True fitness starts on your plate. Every meal is an opportunity to energize your body, sharpen your focus for lectures, and recover stronger after a session at the gym or park. You don't need to be a Michelin-star chef to cook smart—just a few simple, fresh ingredients and recipes designed to fit a busy student lifestyle.

item.title: Student Blog
item.dc:creator: arir71302
item.content:encoded:
Welcome to the Herts Active Student Blog!

Discover simple ways to stay active, eat healthier, improve your wellbeing and enjoy student life without spending too much money.

Whether you're a beginner or already enjoy fitness, we've got useful tips and ideas to help you live a healthier and happier student life.

Explore our latest articles, fitness tips and affordable activities around Hertfordshire!

University life can be exciting, but balancing lectures, assignments, part-time jobs and social activities can sometimes make it difficult to stay healthy.

Staying fit doesn't have to be expensive or time-consuming. Even small changes to your daily routine can make a big difference to your physical and mental wellbeing.

At Herts Active, we believe every student deserves the opportunity to enjoy a healthy and active lifestyle, regardless of their budget.

Here are some simple ways to stay fit while enjoying your university life!

Explore Your Local Parks 🌳

You don't need an expensive gym membership to stay active. Walking, jogging and cycling in local parks are great ways to keep your body moving.

Hertfordshire has many beautiful outdoor spaces where students can enjoy fresh air, exercise and spend time with friends.

Whether you prefer a morning walk or an evening jog, outdoor activities are a great way to stay active without spending money.

Student tip: Invite a friend to join you for a weekend walk and make fitness more enjoyable!

Try Free Home Workouts 💪

Busy with university assignments? Don't worry! You don't always need to visit a gym to stay fit.

Home workouts are a convenient and affordable way to exercise. You can use your bedroom, living room or any small available space.

Here are some beginner-friendly exercises:

  • Squats
  • Push-ups
  • Lunges
  • Planks
  • Jumping jacks

Start slowly and choose exercises that match your fitness level.

Student tip: Try a 15-minute home workout between your study sessions!

Eat Healthy on a Student Budget 🥗

Count your calories before you pick your food at the cafes . University of hertfordshire's cafe display all the calorie count which actually helps students to make the right and effective decision bassed on their BMI and their daily calorie count.

Moreover University of Hertfordshire's cafes provide vageterian and non-vageterian meals along with the options like fish , chicken , beef, egg and lots of fresh produce.

Student tip: Always mix match your meal thats how you can get your best meal at the cheapest rate.

Take Care of Your Mental Wellbeing 🧠

University life can sometimes become stressful because of assignments, exams, financial responsibilities and personal commitments.

Looking after your mental wellbeing is just as important as looking after your physical health.

Here are some simple ways to improve your wellbeing:

  • Get enough sleep every night.
  • Take regular breaks while studying.
  • Spend time with friends and family.
  • Enjoy outdoor activities.
  • Try meditation or relaxation exercises.
  • Talk to someone you trust when you feel stressed.

Remember, you don't have to deal with everything alone. Your university may also offer student wellbeing and support services.

Student tip: Give yourself some time to relax every day. Your wellbeing matters!

Write for Herts Active

Are you a University of Hertfordshire student with a useful idea, experience or tip to share? We welcome article ideas about fitness, local places, student food, sport and wellbeing.

How student submissions work

  • Send an idea: Use the form to share your proposed topic and a short outline. You do not need a WordPress account to send an idea.
  • Editorial review: The Herts Active team reviews submissions and contacts you if the idea is suitable.
  • Draft your article: For accepted contributors, the team can send a WordPress invitation so you can write a draft using your own account.
  • Approval before publishing: An editor reviews the draft, checks links and images, and publishes it when ready. Sending a form does not automatically publish an article.

Before you submit

  • Share original writing and credit sources for facts or quotations.
  • Only submit photos you took yourself or have permission to use.
  • Do not include private health details or personal information about other people.
  • Keep advice respectful, inclusive and suitable for a student audience.

How to submit an idea

At the moment, Herts Active is using an editor-reviewed contributor process rather than open public publishing. Share your proposed topic and a short outline with the Herts Active project team through your agreed university or project communication channel. The editors can then review the idea and invite selected contributors to the site.

Want to write a full article? Once an idea is accepted, a site administrator can invite you to WordPress.com as a Contributor. You will use your own account to create a draft, and the Herts Active editors will review and publish it.

A public submission form can be added once the team chooses a shared inbox for submissions. The form should be tested in Jetpack → Forms before being advertised to visitors, so ideas reach the right people.

Creating a general WordPress.com account does not automatically give you permission to write for Herts Active. The site currently uses the Subscriber role for public registrations; Contributors must be invited by an administrator.

How contributor accounts work

Herts Active can invite selected students as WordPress.com Contributors. A Contributor can create and edit their own draft posts, but cannot publish them or upload media. An editor or site administrator reviews and publishes approved work. Each student uses their own WordPress.com login; passwords should never be shared.

This gives students a way to contribute without opening the website to unmoderated public publishing. The site owner can send invitations from Users → Add New User and choose the Contributor role.

item.title: Hatfield
item.dc:creator: dankzone
item.content:encoded:
Hatfield has several ways to stay active, from university sports facilities and commercial gyms to council-maintained parks and outdoor exercise equipment. This guide highlights useful starting points for students and local residents.

Sports and fitness facilities

Hertfordshire Sports Village

Based at the University of Hertfordshire's de Havilland Campus, the Sports Village offers a large gym, 25-metre swimming pool, climbing wall, studios, racquet courts and indoor and outdoor sports facilities. It is open to students and the wider community, with membership and pay-as-you-go options.

Check facilities and visit options · Read visitor FAQs

Local gyms

Herts Active already has a separate page with Hatfield gym listings, descriptions and the prices previously recorded by the project team.

Check current membership terms and prices directly with each provider before joining, as offers can change.

View Hatfield Gym Listings

Parks, outdoor gyms and open spaces

Hatfield Town Council's facilities directory covers open spaces, play areas, sports facilities and outdoor gym equipment. The council-operated directory currently describes 32 open spaces, 19 play areas and outdoor gym equipment at six locations.

  • Ellenbrook Playing Field and Play Area: local open space with play facilities and outdoor gym equipment.
  • Centenary Park: includes outdoor gym equipment.
  • Acacia Street Recreation and Play Area: includes outdoor gym equipment.
  • Birchwood Leisure Centre and Playing Fields: a local venue for sports and community activities, including football, basketball and badminton.

Browse Hatfield Town Council's official facilities directory for addresses, maps and the latest site information.

item.title: Basic Workout Package
item.dc:creator: dankzone
item.content:encoded:
An affordable starting point for students who want a simple, repeatable fitness routine without needing a gym membership.

Illustrative project price

£3.99 / month

Prototype price only. This is not a live subscription or payment offer.

What's included in the example plan?

  • Three beginner-friendly workout sessions each week.
  • Bodyweight routines that can be completed at home.
  • Warm-up and cool-down guidance for each session.
  • A simple weekly activity planner.
  • A printable progress and habit checklist.

Who is it for?

Students who are starting their fitness journey, prefer home workouts, or want a low-cost structure to help them build a consistent routine.

Example weekly structure: Monday – full-body basics; Wednesday – cardio and movement; Friday – strength and mobility. Adjust sessions to your ability and take rest days when needed.

Educational prototype only. The workouts, features and monthly price are proposed examples for a university project, not a real service currently supplied by Herts Active.

Compare all packages
Try free workouts

item.title: Premium Workout Package
item.dc:creator: dankzone
item.content:encoded:
For students who want more structure and variety, with a gradual plan that can be followed at home or in a gym.

Illustrative project price

£6.99 / month

Prototype price only. This is not a live subscription or payment offer.

What's included in the example plan?

  • Everything in the Basic Package.
  • A sample four-week progressive workout calendar.
  • Home and gym alternatives for key exercises.
  • A balanced mix of strength, cardio and mobility sessions.
  • Exercise substitutions for limited equipment or space.
  • A weekly progress log and planning sheet.

Who is it for?

Students who already exercise occasionally and want a more organised routine, different workout options and a clear way to track progress.

Example weekly structure: two strength sessions, one cardio session, one mobility or recovery session, with rest days between harder workouts.

Educational prototype only. The workouts, features and monthly price are proposed examples for a university project, not a real service currently supplied by Herts Active.

Compare all packages
Try free workouts

item.title: Exclusive Workout Package
item.dc:creator: dankzone
item.content:encoded:
The most complete example tier for students who want a wider exercise library and more detailed planning options.

Illustrative project price

£9.99 / month

Prototype price only. This is not a live subscription or payment offer.

What's included in the example plan?

  • Everything in the Premium Package.
  • An example eight-week training calendar with beginner, intermediate and more challenging variations.
  • Separate strength, cardio, mobility and active-recovery sessions.
  • Exercise alternatives for home, gym and outdoor spaces.
  • A more detailed weekly planner and progress review checklist.
  • Guidance for adapting sessions around a busy study timetable.

Who is it for?

Students who enjoy structured training and want a larger selection of routines and planning resources. The example plan is still self-guided; it does not include personal coaching or medical advice.

Example weekly structure: two strength sessions, one cardio session, one mobility or recovery session and one optional outdoor activity, with flexibility for rest and study commitments.

Educational prototype only. The workouts, features and monthly price are proposed examples for a university project, not a real service currently supplied by Herts Active.
